text.p: Frankfurt city has banned a neo-Nazi demonstration against a controversial exhibition about the German army's role in Nazi war crimes, police said on Friday.
They said municipal authorities had denied permission to neo-Nazis to hold a meeting outside the city's St Paul's church on Sunday, when exhibition is due to open.
But they said a planned vigil by the right-wing Repulican party outside St Paul's on Monday was not affected by the ban.
The exhibition stirred debate when it was unveiled in Hamburg two years ago and clashes erupted between neo-Nazis and left-wing activists when it was shown in Munich last month.

It uses photographs and letters from soldiers to support its claim that the regular army, as well as the SS units usually blamed for war crimes, took part in the mass killings of Jews and other wartime atrocities.
